title: For beta greater than three the coherent Wick quartic gives a semibounded strong-resolvent interacting Hamiltonian

interacting_control.regime: beta>3, g>=0, normalized T3, with covariance q_beta and H_beta=dGamma(omega^beta) from K1447
interacting_control.finite_variance: C_beta=sum_k (2 omega_k^beta)^(-1) is finite, and C_(beta,N) increases to C_beta
interacting_control.counterterms: V_(beta,N)=integral(phi_N^4-6 C_(beta,N) phi_N^2+3 C_(beta,N)^2) dx; these are exactly the Wick quadratic and vacuum counterterms
interacting_control.uniform_lower_bound: For every real x, x^4-6Cx^2+3C^2>=-6C^2, so V_(beta,N)>=-6 C_beta^2
interacting_control.limit: K1447 at s=0 gives V_(beta,N) convergence in L2(mu_beta), hence in L1, to V_beta
interacting_control.closed_forms: h_(beta,N)+g V_(beta,N) and h_beta+g V_beta on D(h_beta) intersect D((V_beta+6C_beta^2)^(1/2)) are densely defined, closed and bounded below by -6g C_beta^2
interacting_control.strong_resolvent: In Gaussian Q-space the H_beta Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Feynman--Kac formula applies. Stationarity gives E integral_0^t |V_N-V|(X_tau)d tau=t||V_N-V||_1; the common lower bound dominates the exponentials, so semigroups and therefore resolvents converge strongly
interacting_control.ceiling: This is a genuine full Wick-potential construction only in the explicitly UV-softened beta>3 representation. It is not the beta=1 theory, a GU-source Hamiltonian, an interacting BRST theorem, or physical-cohomology admission
